passage:
"Chetan, it's bath time."
"NO!" Chetan threw himself down, kicking.
Saurabh knelt down. His voice went low. "You are upset. I am here."
"No bath! No!"
Saurabh quietly moved the toy truck away from Chetan's feet.
"I'm right here."
Chetan screamed and kicked. Saurabh didn't argue. He just waited, close by.
After a while, Chetan's screams got smaller.

qa.q: What did Saurabh move away from Chetan's feet?
qa.a: He moved the toy truck away from Chetan's feet.

qa.q: What did Chetan feel when it was bath time?
qa.a: He felt angry and upset because he did not want a bath.

qa.q: What did Saurabh do that helped Chetan most?
qa.a: He knelt, spoke in a low voice, kept things safe and waited without arguing, showing Chetan that big feelings can pass.

qa.q: How might Saurabh feel while waiting close by as Chetan screams?
qa.a: Saurabh may find the screaming hard to hear, but stays calm and patient, trusting that Chetan's big feelings will pass.

grounding: It shows a caregiver kneeling, saying you are upset, I am here in a low voice, moving objects aside and waiting without argument.

passage:
Daycare note, Friday.
At nap time Omkar (2) had a big tantrum. He lay on the mat, crying and hitting the floor. I knelt near him. I said softly, "You are upset. I am here." I moved the water bottle and blocks away. I did not argue. I just stayed. Slowly his crying got softer. He crawled to me. 🤍
— Hemant, teacher

qa.q: Where did Omkar lie during his tantrum?
qa.a: He lay on the mat.

qa.q: What does Omkar crawling to Hemant show?
qa.a: It shows Omkar felt safe and wanted comfort once the storm eased.

qa.q: Why did Hemant's way work?
qa.a: Hemant stayed close, kept things safe and did not argue, so Omkar learned his big feelings could pass.

qa.q: How might Omkar's parents feel reading this note?
qa.a: They may feel grateful that the teacher stayed calm and close with Omkar.

grounding: It illustrates a teacher kneeling, saying you are upset, I am here, moving objects aside and waiting quietly, which shows big feelings are survivable.

passage:
In the village courtyard, little Hrithik lay crying and kicking because Dada had taken away the sickle he'd picked up.

Jagdish Dada didn't argue. He moved the sickle and a heavy pot far out of reach. Then he knelt down in the dust.

"You are upset," he said, low and slow. "I am here."

Hrithik kept kicking. Dada didn't talk more. He just stayed close.

After a while the kicking stopped. Hrithik lay there, hiccuping, looking at Dada's knees.

qa.q: What had Hrithik picked up?
qa.a: A sickle.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling as he cried and kicked?
qa.a: He was angry and upset that the sickle was taken away.

qa.q: Why was Jagdish Dada's approach helpful?
qa.a: He moved dangerous things away, knelt nearby, spoke calmly and waited without arguing, showing big feelings are survivable.

qa.q: What might Jagdish Dada be feeling as he waits in the dust?
qa.a: He may feel worried after seeing the sickle, but calm and patient, trusting that staying close will help.

grounding: Jagdish Dada moves dangerous objects away, kneels and says "You are upset. I am here", staying close without argument until toddler Hrithik calms.

passage:
In their Berlin kitchen, Soo-ah threw herself down, screaming and kicking, because Selin wouldn't let her hold the hot teapot.

Selin moved the chair away and pushed the teapot to the back of the counter. Then she knelt down.

"You are upset. I am here," she said softly.

Soo-ah screamed louder. Selin didn't argue or explain. She stayed close and calm, near her daughter.

Slowly, the screams turned to sobs.

qa.q: What did Soo-ah want to hold?
qa.a: The hot teapot.

qa.q: How did Soo-ah feel when Selin said no?
qa.a: She felt angry and frustrated, screaming and kicking on the floor.

qa.q: What did Selin do that helped Soo-ah through the storm?
qa.a: She moved the chair and teapot out of the way, knelt close, spoke softly and waited without arguing.

qa.q: What might Selin be feeling as she waits?
qa.a: She may feel tired or tense, but she stays calm to show Soo-ah that big feelings can be survived.

grounding: Selin moves harmful objects aside, kneels and says "You are upset. I am here", staying close without argument until toddler Soo-ah's screams turn to sobs.

passage:
I'm Santosh, Hrithik's neighbour. Last Sunday I saw his mother do something new to me.

Hrithik lay on their doorstep, kicking near the stairs, screaming because she'd taken her scissors back.

She didn't shout. She moved him gently back from the edge, put the scissors on a high shelf, and knelt beside him. "You are upset. I am here," she said, very quietly.

Then she just waited. No lecture.

Soon Hrithik crawled into her lap. I'll remember that.

qa.q: What had Hrithik's mother taken back?
qa.a: Her scissors.

qa.q: How did Santosh feel watching Hrithik's mother?
qa.a: Santosh was surprised and impressed, wanting to remember what she did.

qa.q: Why did the mother's response work?
qa.a: She made him safe by moving him from the stairs and the scissors away, stayed close and calm, and waited without lecturing.

qa.q: How might Hrithik feel crawling into his mother's lap?
qa.a: He probably feels calmer and comforted, knowing she was there through his big feelings.

grounding: Santosh, a neighbour, observes a mother move harmful things aside, kneel and say "You are upset. I am here", staying close until her toddler calms.

passage:
Monday. Eshaan, two, threw himself down when the TV went off. Tarun knelt. "You're upset. I'm here." He moved the glass cup away and waited.
Wednesday. Another storm, over shoes. Tarun knelt again, quiet and close. Eshaan kicked, then slowed sooner.
Saturday. Bath time ended. Eshaan wailed, then crawled straight into Tarun's lap, still sobbing, and let himself be held.

qa.q: What did Tarun move away on Monday?
qa.a: He moved the glass cup away.

qa.q: Why did Eshaan crawl into Tarun's lap on Saturday?
qa.a: He still felt upset, but he had come to feel safe with Tarun close by, so he looked for comfort sooner.

qa.q: What in Tarun's approach seems to help each time?
qa.a: Kneeling close, saying calmly 'You're upset. I'm here', moving dangerous things away and waiting without arguing.

qa.q: What might Tarun feel as the storms get shorter?
qa.a: Tarun may feel relieved and encouraged that staying calm and close is helping.

grounding: Shows a caregiver kneeling close, speaking softly, moving harmful objects and waiting, and a toddler learning that big feelings can be survived.
